minutes.headline: Board declined to put the Community Preservation Act on the June town meeting and pressed for a more cautious budget.
minutes.summary: The board heard from the Historical Commission about putting the Community Preservation Act on the annual town meeting warrant. Three members said they would not support it now, and the proponent was given a week to consult her group. Members also debated how conservative the town manager's budget is, with sharp exchanges. A bicycle charity ride was approved with conditions, and public comment covered tax-bill penalties and the DPW fuel tank location.

what_happened.line: Three members said they would not support the Community Preservation Act on the warrant now; the proponent has a week to consult her group before a vote.
Members debated how conservative the town manager's FY21 budget is, including state aid and new growth assumptions; nothing was resolved and it continues next week.
The board voted 3-0 to approve a bicycle charity ride, conditioned on the governor's emergency order being lifted and public health conditions allowing.
The DPW fuel tank location will go on a future agenda with stakeholders invited, though not next week; the town manager said a state earmark means no June 30 deadline.
A resident asked for late fees and interest on tax bills to be waived; the town manager said the board had waived them through June 29.

why_it_matters: The Community Preservation Act would add a surcharge to property tax bills if it reaches the June town meeting ballot, and the board's vote next week decides whether the article stays on the warrant.
The budget debate turns on how much cushion the tax levy keeps if state aid or local receipts fall short, which affects the size of next year's tax bill and the services it pays for.
The fuel tank siting touches a riverfront area near homes, and residents will have a chance to weigh in when it is scheduled.
watch_next: Next week's Select Board meeting: vote on keeping the CPA article on the warrant, then budget first, warrant articles, and a joint session with legislators.
Members seeking budget cuts are asked to bring specific lists to next week's meeting.

reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the bicycle ride vote, the CPA surcharge figures, levy capacity, new growth, the 1.58% school increase and the core attendees. The CPA decision is the main difference: ours has the board voting next meeting on keeping the CPA article on the warrant, while the official minutes say the CPA ballot question was passed over because of state deadlines.
